thread:
oliver: Quick Q — assembling SLA report for acme-inc. Need tenant-level uptime numbers and a pointer to the dashboard/good queries. Also noticed burn-rate alerts for 502s around 03:20 UTC last night, any tips on where to look? Thanks.
maria: For uptime use Console -> Service Health -> Tenant Metrics -> 'Uptime by Tenant' (filters at top). permalink: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/service-health/uptime-by-tenant : there's a tenant filter. That view uses the metric redwood_http_requests_total with `status=~\"2..|3..|4..\"` split — uptime = 1 - errors/total.
alex: If you want the raw PromQL: `1 - sum(rate(redwood_http_requests_total{tenant=\"acme-inc\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_http_requests_total{tenant=\"acme-inc\"}[5m]))`. Change window to 1m/10m depending on spike smoothing.
jess: For the 502s check the traces page, filter by service=frontend and http.status_code=502, look for `route=/api/generate` and model shard timeouts. If traces aren't sampled, use logs: query `service:frontend status:502 tenant:acme-inc` in Logs->Live.
alerts-bot: Alert triggered: SLO burn-rate (acme-inc) — 502 spike — burn-rate=3.2x over 1h window. Incident link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-1123
oliver: Nice, thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Should we adjust alert sensitivity for acme-inc (they get occasional retries)? 2) Any quick guardrails to avoid noisy burn-rate alerts (grouping / label tweaks)?
maria: For noisy tenants you can change the burn-rate alert to group by (tenant, route) and require min request volume: add `and sum(rate(...[5m])) by (tenant) > 50` so tiny tenants don't trigger. Also consider increasing evaluation window from 5m->15m.
alex: Also filter out known retry responses by excluding `x-retry=true` header if we set it on retries: `redwood_http_requests_total{tenant=\"acme-inc\",retry!\=\"true\"}`. If you can't set header, look for `user_agent` or `retry_reason` tag.
jess: If the 502s are backend timeouts, we recommend a fallback policy: route to smaller model or lower max_tokens for that tenant. Ops can create a canary route that returns 503->fallback automatically.
oliver: Can someone paste the exact dashboard permalink with the tenant filter set so I can embed in the report?
maria: Pasting permalink with tenant pre-filter: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/service-health/uptime-by-tenant?tenant=acme-inc — should land you there. :thumbsup:
alex: Also FYI, there's a per-tenant alert suppression rule we can enable for enterprise accounts (contact support). It's in Console -> Alerts -> Suppressions.
jess: I'll pull the traces and attach a couple trace IDs here in a follow-up comment. If anyone wants to look in the meantime, check the latency heatmap on the dashboard to correlate 502s with GC spikes.
oliver: Great — appreciate it. If jess posts traces I can add them to the SLA appendix.
